summary: Jay L. Garfield is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied with teachers including Geshe Ngawang Samten and Robert A. F. Thurman. He held posts at Hampshire College, Smith College, and the National University of Singapore.
Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar. He served as a Reader of Sanskrit at Gujarat University.

Jayandra Soni is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed Ph.D. degrees at Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University. He was a lecturer at the University of Marburg from 1991 to 2012.
Jayanta Acharya is an Indology scholar who earned a PhD at Nepal Sanskrit University, where he became a professor in 1997. He also served with the International Astronomical Union from 2009 to 2018.

Jayashree D. Sathe is a scholar in Indology and linguistics affiliated with the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where she has served as editor in chief (attested 2011) and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

Jaś Elsner is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies who earned his PhD from King's College, Cambridge. He has held posts at the Courtauld Institute of Art and the University of Oxford.

Jean Arzoumanov works in Indology and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he has been affiliated with the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and served as a Rocher Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Chicago.

Jean Boisselier was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Philippe Stern and Pierre Dupont. He served as Conservator at the National Museum of Cambodia and later taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle University.

Jean Buhot was a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and sinology. He served as Professor of Chinese and Japanese Art at the École du Louvre (1936) and Professor of Japanese at INALCO (1940).

Jean Carl was a specialist in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1928–1931) and the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (~1936–1941).

Jean Dantinne is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Liège and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He held teaching posts at the University of Liège (1975) and Université catholique de Louvain (1983).

Jean Deloche was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar. He directed the Alliance Française of Madras and served as a researcher and associate member at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Deny was a linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. He later taught there (~1908–1949), at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, and at Georgetown University.

Jean Ferdinand Caius was an Indologist and scientist educated at the University of Paris and Jesuit theological colleges. He served as a pharmacologist at the Haffkine Institute and as a teacher and researcher at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai.
Jean Fezas is an Indology scholar who held positions in Sanskrit language and literature at Sorbonne Nouvelle University, attested in 1996 and 2007.

Jean Filliozat was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Renou. He held posts at the Collège de France, the EPHE, and directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Jean Haudry was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Armand Minard. He held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Jean Moulin University - Lyon 3.

Jean Herbert was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Sri Aurobindo in 1934. He served with the League of Nations and the United Nations, and taught Eastern Mythologies at the University of Geneva (1954–1964).

Jean Kellens is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Karl Hoffmann. He held posts at the University of Liège, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, and the Collège de France.

Jean Naudou was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Paris. He served as a Sanskrit specialist at the Université libre de Bruxelles from 1967 to 1976.
